evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

independent_computation.question: Is Syndra's E an intrinsic stun, or is its stun conditional on a Dark Sphere (i.e. does the rotation order E-after-Q follow from a declared enabler)?

steps.claim: E's own cone applies knockback + magic damage, NOT a stun.
steps.quote: Active: Syndra propels a wave of force in a cone in the target direction that deals magic damage to enemies hit and knocks them back for 400 units and up to 800 units away from Syndra based on proximity, though not through terrain.
steps.note: The word 'stun' does not appear anywhere in this first (base-cast) effect row. Damage row is 60/95/130/165/200 (+60% AP).

steps.claim: The 1.25 s stun exists only on the sphere-collision branch of E: a Dark Sphere must already be on the ground for E to push into an enemy.
steps.quote: Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units and up to 1200 units away from Syndra based on proximity, knocking back enemies they hit over 70 units, though not through terrain. Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds, during which they are also revealed, and dealt Scatter the Weak's damage if they were not damaged by the initial cast.

steps.claim: Dark Spheres are produced by Q (Dark Sphere); Q is the only sphere-producing ability that can precede E in a Q -> W -> E -> R rotation.
quotes: Q: 'Active: Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location that appears after a 0.6-second delay, dealing magic damage to nearby enemies. The Dark Sphere then remains on the ground for 6 seconds.'
W: 'Active: Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster ...' -- W consumes/relocates an existing sphere, it does not create one.

R: 'Active: Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones ...' / 'The Dark Spheres will then remain on the ground next to the target's current location for 6 seconds.' -- R also creates spheres, but R is cast after E in the rotation.
steps.note: Sphere lifetime is 6 s, comfortably longer than the E cooldown gap inside one rotation, so a Q-placed sphere is live when E is cast.

steps.claim: The Transcendent (P) bonus on E is a 70% slow, and it is explicitly described as starting AFTER the stun 'if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere' -- confirming the stun is the pushed-sphere branch, not the cone.
steps.quote: Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 80 Splinters of Wrath enhances Scatter the Weak to have an increased scatter angle and slow enemies hit by 70% for 1.25 seconds starting after the knock back ends or if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere, after the stun has ended.

steps.claim: Conclusion: the correct rotation-order source for E's CC is a declared enabler edge 'E requires Q', not an intrinsic cc_kind='stun' on E.
steps.reasoning: E cast with no Dark Sphere on the ground produces zero stun (steps 1, 4). The stun is entirely a property of the Q-created sphere being pushed (steps 2, 3). A rotation-ordering justification that reads 'E has cc_kind=stun' asserts an unconditional property the source text does not grant, and it hides the actual reason E must follow Q; the enabler declaration states exactly the prerequisite the wiki text supports. Both values ultimately order E after Q, but only the new one is derivable from the cached source rather than from a module-authored QE-combo assumption.

independent_computation.caveat: Strictly, R also creates Dark Spheres and leaves them on the ground for 6 s, so E's stun is enabled by 'a live Dark Sphere' in general, not by Q uniquely. Within the derived cast order under test (Q before W before E before R), Q is the only sphere source that precedes E, so 'E requires Q' is the correct enabler edge for this scenario. If a scenario ever derives an order where R precedes E, the enabler set should read {Q, R}.

"E/W CC (stun, knockback, slow - utility only)"; "cc (E stun/knockback, W slow, 11 atoms)" -- corroborates that E carries both a knockback (cone) and a stun (sphere) branch, modeled as utility.

"Ability recasts are scheduled on one shared timeline ... the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order." No cc_kind / cc_enabler semantics are defined anywhere in this document (grep for 'cc_enabler', 'cc_kind', 'stun', 'crowd control' returns nothing), so the ordering justification must come from the cached ability text, which it now does.

notes: Could not independently verify the revision id 4024662 in the citation; data/wiki/article-index.json records only pageid 641379 for 'Syndra' and carries no revision ids. The quoted ability text itself is verifiable and matches the new value's claim.

The old value is not factually false about a stun existing on E -- it is wrong as a *rotation-order source*: it presents an unconditional module-authored cc_kind where the cached text conditions the stun on a pre-placed Dark Sphere, i.e. on Q.
